newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares forge ahead amid company news flood.
newsitem.headline: German shares forge ahead amid company news flood.

text.p: A flood of positively received corporate news and strong overnight performances on U.S. and Japanese stock markets triggered a broad advance to fresh record highs on the German share market early on Tuesday.

In pre-bourse electronic trade the IBIS DAX index vaulted for the first time over the psychologically crucial 3,600 point level in the early minutes of dealing before easing back somewhat to trade at 3,598.12 points at 0721 GMT, up 32.43.
"All the news has been positive today," said a Frankfurt dealer. "Wall Street was good, the Nikkei was better and we are simply keeping up."
Heading the field was diversified energy and telecommunications group Veba AG, boosted by a first quarter earnings report that dealers said was significatly above expectations.
Adidas AG was also among the morning's outperformers after reporting first quarter data which was taken positively in the market.

Other corporate news expected today includes a possible dividend announcement from airline Lufthansa AG, news from building firm Hochtief AG 's annual news conference and Hoechst AG's shareholder meeting.
Veba's shares topped turnover volumes in early pre-bourse trade as they rose 3.35 marks, or 3.7 percent to 93.55 marks, making it the top gainer among blue chip stocks.
"It looks like Veba will be the stock of the day," said one dealer. "The numbers were significantly above forecasts."
Veba had said it expected to be able to raise its profits for 1997 as it continues to take measures to cut costs and improve efficiency.
The company also said its first quarter net profit after minorities rose seven percent to 486 million marks while pre-tax profit rose 6.8 percent to 1.08 billion marks.
Adidas shares were up 3.6 percent at 186.50 marks.
The sports retailer said earlier its net profit rose 33 percent in the first quarter.
Among the few losers was SGL Carbon AG, which dropped on thin turnover after reporting a nine percent drop in first quarter pre-tax profit.
